title: Whiskey Date Cake

ingredientGroups.title: Date cake
items: 1 (8 oz) package dried pitted dates, chopped into ½-inch pieces

steps: Date cake: Heat oven to 350°. Combine dates, baking soda and boiling water; soak 15–20 minutes. Process the date mixture for 2 minutes to form a paste.

Cream the butter in a stand mixer for about 1 minute. Add sugar and cream 3 minutes more. Scrape the bowl; add eggs one at a time, mixing between additions. Mix in the flour on low speed, about ½ cup at a time, just until incorporated. Fold in the date paste.

Spray an 8 × 14-inch cake pan and coat its bottom and sides with turbinado sugar. Pour in batter and bake 30–40 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool 20 minutes; turn onto a parchment-lined tray and cool completely.

Optional self-rising flour blend from the source: mix 3 cups all-purpose flour, 2 tsp iodized salt and 1 Tbsp baking powder. Use immediately or keep airtight; measure the 1¾ cups needed for the cake from the blend.

Bourbon sauce: Bring cream, ¼ cup sugar and vanilla bean to a simmer. Whisk the yolks and remaining ¼ cup sugar until frothy. Slowly whisk in half the hot cream, then return to the pot and cook over medium-low until thick enough to coat a spoon.

Stir in vanilla extract and bourbon; remove from heat, strain and cool in an ice bath. Use immediately or refrigerate; if chilled, reheat at 50% microwave power in 10-second intervals until slightly warm and pourable.

Toffee sauce: Melt butter over medium heat, add brown sugar and cook about 8 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add cream and cook 6–7 minutes more. Remove from heat and stir in bourbon and vanilla. Use immediately or refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat before use.

Spiced pecans: Heat oven to 350°. Mix water, syrup, salt and peppers; toss with pecans to coat. Spread on a foil-lined baking sheet and bake 12–15 minutes. Scrape from the pan and break up clumps immediately; cool completely. Store airtight at room temperature.
Whipped cream: Whip cream, sugar and vanilla, starting at low speed and increasing to high, until slightly stiff peaks form. Use immediately or refrigerate.

To serve: Cut cake into 12 pieces and poke several holes in each. Place on a nonstick foil-lined baking sheet. Heat oven to 500° and pour ¼ cup toffee sauce over each piece. Warm for 4–5 minutes, until bubbling.
Spoon ¼ cup bourbon sauce onto each plate; add warm cake, whipped cream and spiced pecans.
reviewFlags: The source contains two different versions. This is its separately labeled 12-serving alternate; confirm whether the nine-serving original should also be included. The source lists oven temperatures in degrees without a temperature scale.
